newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to press for reform of IMF, World Bank.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to press for reform of IMF, World Bank.

text.p: A Labour government would push for reform of the IMF and World Bank to put more emphasis on tackling poverty, Joan Lestor, the party's former overseas development spokeswoman, said on Thursday.

"We will insist that their programmes make measurable progress towards the elimination of poverty. That means an end to traditional forms of structral adjustment, and a new emphasis on investment in people -- in health and education," Lestor, who is retiring at the next election, said.

She also told the main opposition party's annual conference that a Labour government would start to reverse the decline in Britain's aid budget, which has shrunk under the ruling Conservatives, and would focus aid on the poorest countries.
"And we will also take new inititives to further reduce the debt burden faced by the poorest countries," Lestor said.
The party's new overseas development spokeswoman, Clare Short, said Labour would press the IMF and World Bank to promote human development "rather than ruthless, jobless growth".
She said Labour was committed to meeting the U.N. aid target of 0.7 percent of GNP and would increase its aid programme as the British economy grew.
"Aid is not a substitute for economic strategies to eliminate poverty but must be part of that strategy," she said.
